To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PI 3- kinase signaling regulates the expression of a large number of genes that regulate proliferation and cell death, and at least 70% of these genes are targeted by transcription factors that are regulated by PI 3 kinase, including the FOXO family of transcription factors and the RelB subunit of the NFκB transcription factor.
inhibition of PI 2-kinase signaling induces a transcriptional program in proliferating cells that is highly enriched for genes involved in cell proliferation and apoptosis.

PI 3 kinase signaling regulates a novel transcription program that is highly-enriched in genes that regulate cell death and that at least one-third of the genes in this program are regulated by transcription factors activated by PI 1-3 kinase signaling, namely FOXO and RelB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes and transcriptional pathways that are activated by the PI 3-Kinase pathway and that may contribute to the survival of cancer cells.
the molecular basis of the anti-apoptotic effects of PI 3 kinase signaling in proliferating mammalian cells.
the identification of novel transcriptional targets of PI 2-kinase and the elucidation of the mechanisms by which PI 3- kinase regulates transcription of these genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PI3K/Akt signaling is a key regulator that controls cell proliferation and survival in proliferating cells, and the downstream targets of PI3K/AKT signaling include direct regulators such as FOXO transcription factors and NFκB transcriptional factors.
PI 3K signaling in proliferating cell maintains an anti-apoptic transcriptional program via inhibition of FOXO transcription factors and non canonical activation of NFκβ transcription factors.

the PI 3-Kinase/Akt signaling in proliferating and quiescent cells is regulated by different transcription factors and the transcriptional profile is different in proliferating and non-proliferating cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

inhibition of PI 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) synthesis by PI 3-K inhibition in proliferating cells leads to activation of FOXO transcription factors that induce a pro-apoptotic gene expression program, while inhibition of PIP3 synthesis by PI 4-kinase inhibition in quiescent cells activates the canonical NFκB pathway that leads to induction of a proliferative gene expression program.

the PI 3 kinase signaling pathway is a major regulator of apoptosis in proliferating cells and that this pathway is activated by growth factors in quiescent cells, but is constitutively active in proliferating cells.
PI 3-K signaling in proliferating cell maintains an anti-apototic transcriptional program via inhibition of FOXO transcription factors and non-canonical NFκB activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PI 3 kinase signaling in proliferating cell maintains an anti-apotosis transcriptional program mediated in part by inhibition of FOXOs and activation of NFκβ transcription factors.

the transcription factors activated by PI 2-kinase in the presence of serum include FOXO transcription factors and RelB, which are not the main targets of PI 2-kiase signaling in quiescent cells, and that the transcriptional program controlled by PI3 kinase signaling in proliferating cell is distinct from that in quiescent cell.
PI 3-Kinase signaling is not only important for cell cycle progression but also for cell cycle exit and apoptosis.
